clue.text: Fancy the accountant wanting a fee!

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
a fee is the price charged

explanation.surface: Someone imagines their accountant asking for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is the definition as a noun: a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim, which is one sense of the noun fancy.

clue.text: Criticise clothes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to attack or batter, informally
second meaning: British slang for gear or garments

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British informal usage: to give someone a beating, and one's belongings or garments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for laying into someone verbally and for the gear a person wears.

clue.text: Sons of the soil locking each son in the larder

indicators.note: something locking a thing in shuts it inside

parts.note: a pantry is a larder
ea is the abbreviation for each
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Farm workers lock each boy in the food store.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry are the rural class who work the land, poetically sons of the soil.

clue.text: Thoughts scattered by Sadie

indicators.note: things scattered are spread about in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Sadie spreads her notions around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions formed in the mind, which is what thoughts are.

clue.text: Quilt is done wider when repaired

indicators.note: something repaired has been reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bedcover is made bigger after mending.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick quilt, originally stuffed with the down of eider ducks.

clue.text: Protection underneath when there's a cooker to fix

parts.note: a hob is the cooking top of a stove
to nail something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Someone advises putting a protective mat beneath the stove before repairing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A hobnail is a heavy-headed nail driven into the sole of a boot to protect it from wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobnails guard the underside of boot soles, so they are protection worn underneath.

clue.text: It lets door move in hospital that is no good inside

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another is held within it

parts.note: i.e. is Latin id est, that is
NG is short for no good

explanation.surface: A hospital door won't open properly and something is wrong inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivoting joint that allows a door to swing open and shut.

clue.text: Money containers?

parts.note: surface reading: purses, wallets or safes
setter's reading: bread is slang for money, so these are kitchen boxes for loaves

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so the kitchen containers for loaves become money containers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are kitchen containers for loaves, and bread is a slang term for cash.

clue.text: A Liberal, one called in defence

parts.note: taken as written
Lib is short for Liberal
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is summoned as a witness for the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one called in defence' reads together, but 'one' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that the accused was elsewhere, invoked as a defence in court.

clue.text: Passenger ship, keel half hidden, one familiar with pitches

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped
something hidden is tucked inside something else

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
the first half of keel

explanation.surface: A ship whose keel is partly out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Lineker is a former England footballer and TV presenter; 'pitches' are football pitches, not a ship's pitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary Lineker spent his career on football pitches, so is a person familiar with them.

clue.text: Having nothing to consider, speak!

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
to rate is to consider or regard

explanation.surface: An impatient demand that someone with no thoughts should talk anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally, as in delivering a speech.

clue.text: Blow this clock, children!

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to destroy or blow on a timepiece
setter's reading: the fluffy seed head of a weed, which children blow to 'tell the time'

explanation.walkthrough: The 'clock' is the round puffball of seeds on a common yellow-flowered weed; children blow it and count the puffs to tell the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed head of this weed is traditionally called a clock, and children blow it away.

clue.text: Money taken by lake-side restaurant

parts.note: brass is informal British slang for money
Erie, one of the Great Lakes, set beside the first part

explanation.surface: Cash is collected at a restaurant by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lake-side' reads as one descriptive word, but the lake is placed at the side of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant serving simple food and drink.

clue.text: A doctor in a thousand wants booze

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A rare doctor who fancies a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcohol, and to booze is to drink it.

clue.text: Correspondence about a riot

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters are being written about a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' looks like letters, but here it means a proportional relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses how one quantity corresponds in proportion to another.

clue.text: Corrupt bosses I have fixed

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have dealt with crooked managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like the end of a sentence about sorting out bosses; it is the definition, meaning fixated.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive mind is fixated on one thing, which is the sense of fixed here.

clue.text: His clothes are unfashionable and more correct

parts.note: out of fashion, so out
fitter means more fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A man's clothes are old-fashioned yet more appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'His clothes' points to the man whose clothes these are because he sells them.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a tradesman who supplies clothing, so the clothes on sale are his.

clue.text: Passes over uplifting painting etc and poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: painting and similar crafts are art
poetry is written in verses

explanation.surface: Someone moves past inspiring pictures and poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross or travel over, so traverses means passes over.

clue.text: Prize trophy mounted, being of high quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means climbing upward, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a prize is a reward
a pot is slang for a sporting trophy cup

explanation.surface: A prize cup put on a stand is of excellent quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the very best class, as of the highest quality.

clue.text: Cracked basin, I say, found in Ethiopia once

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at finding a broken bowl in Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the former name of the country now known as Ethiopia.

clue.text: Comedian, yesterday's leader previously

parts.note: Al Read was a popular British radio comedian of the 1950s

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of yesterday

explanation.surface: A comic who was yesterday's star in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Read was a Lancashire comedian famous on BBC radio in the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time or before now, so it can stand for previously.

clue.text: Dark brown pig with no tail in sea

indicators.note: a word losing its tail loses its last letter
one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
pig with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A tailless brown pig swimming in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish dark brown colour, originally from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Director-general tucked into a cheese, which is cut

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: a plus Brie, the soft French cheese
DG is the abbreviation for Director-General

explanation.surface: A boss eats some cheese that has been sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it signals placing one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, so it means cut as a verb.

clue.text: Fashions for Queen taking a long time

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: Clothes for the monarch take forever to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a verb or clothes, but it means crazes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rages are passing crazes, as in 'all the rage', so they are fashions.

clue.text: Unhealthy and still uncured

definitions.meaning: second meaning: of bacon or timber, not yet cured or seasoned

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a patient not yet recovered, but 'uncured' refers to bacon or wood that has not been preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes a nauseous complexion and also unseasoned wood or unsmoked bacon.

clue.text: Banker certain to be seen in a type of shirt with tail

parts.note: as in T-shirt

indicators.note: a thing seen in something else appears inside it

parts.note: the rear is the tail end
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A banker is sure to be spotted wearing a shirt with a long back.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after an organisation's funds, so is its banker.

clue.text: Detectives in stories we could hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: stories are tales

explanation.surface: Detectives feature in stories we might listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail is someone who follows a suspect secretly, a detective's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails are people who shadow suspects, so detectives tracking someone.

clue.text: A fight taking place in a Dorset town

indicators.note: something taking place in words is located within their letters

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in a southern English county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in southern England; the answer runs across its end and the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief, heated argument or fight.

clue.text: Chaps in first-class neckwear with pleasant features

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
chaps are men
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Smartly dressed men in top-quality ties look good.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a standard term for first-rate; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are agreeable facilities or attractive aspects of a place.

clue.text: Pulled by another to get spliced

parts.note: taken as written
spliced is slang for married

explanation.surface: A boat hauled by another so that a rope can be joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spliced' looks nautical with the towing, but it is informal British for married.
explanation.definitionFit: Something towed has been hauled along by another vehicle or vessel.

clue.text: Americans look for no retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to seek is to look for
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Americans aim for a battle without any retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is an informal name, used chiefly abroad, for people from the United States.

clue.text: Flog small company on demand

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Co is the abbreviation for company
to urge is to press or demand

explanation.surface: Sell off a little firm whenever asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' suggests selling, British slang, but here it means to whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip someone severely, so it means flog in the punishment sense.
